studies.Reference: Consumption of flaxseed, a rich source of lignans, is associated with reduced breast cancer risk.
studies.Authors: Lowcock EC, Cotterchio M, Boucher BA
studies.comparison_type: Yes vs No (weekly consumption of flaxseed vs none)
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: A food frequency questionnaire was used to measure the consumption of flaxseed and flax bread

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 2,999 women with breast cancer and 3,370 healthy control women
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Consumption of flaxseed was associated with a significant reduction in breast cancer risk (odds ratio (OR) = 0.82, 95 % confidence interval (CI) 0.69-0.97)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Consumption of flaxseed was associated with a significant reduction in breast cancer risk
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.022.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: intake of flaxseed-the richest source of dietary lignans (a class of phytoestrogens)
